problem.text: How many nonnegative integers can be written in the form $$a_7\cdot3^7+a_6\cdot3^6+a_5\cdot3^5+a_4\cdot3^4+a_3\cdot3^3+a_2\cdot3^2+a_1\cdot3^1+a_0\cdot3^0,$$ where $a_i\in\{-1,0,1\}$ for $0\le i\le 7$?

steps.title: Where to start: shift the digits to look like base 3
steps.body:
Powers of $3$ with three possible digits look almost like base 3, except the digits are $-1, 0, 1$ instead of $0, 1, 2$. So add $1$ to every digit. That adds $M=1+3+3^2+\cdots+3^7$ to the expression, and turns it into an ordinary base-3 number $N$ with $8$ digits.
$$\text{expression}=N-M$$

your_turn.prompt: Which whole numbers can an $8$-digit base-3 number $N$ (leading zeros allowed) be?
your_turn.answer: Every number from $0$ to $3^8-1=6560$, each written in exactly one way.

steps.title: The values are symmetric around 0
steps.body: So the expression takes every integer from $-M$ to $6560-M$, each exactly once. Writing $3M-M$ makes almost everything cancel, so $2M=3^8-1$, and the top end $(3^8-1)-M$ equals $M$. The values run from $-M$ to $M$ with no gaps.

your_turn.prompt: Try a tiny version with only two digits: which values can $a_1\cdot 3+a_0$ take, and how many are nonnegative?
your_turn.answer: Every integer from $-4$ to $4$, which is $9$ values, and $5$ of them ($0$ to $4$) are nonnegative.

steps.title: Count all the values
steps.body: Each choice of digits gives a different value, so the number of values equals the number of digit choices. Careful: the digits are $a_0$ through $a_7$, which is $8$ digits, not $7$.

your_turn.prompt: How many different values does the full expression take?
your_turn.answer: $3^8=6561$, since each of the $8$ digits has $3$ choices.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The $6561$ values are the integers from $-M$ to $M$, so $M=\frac{6561-1}{2}=3280$. The nonnegative ones are $0, 1, \ldots, 3280$, which is $3281$ numbers. The answer is **(D)**.

wrong_choices.C: $1094=\frac{3^7+1}{2}$ comes from using only $7$ digits. The digits run from $a_0$ to $a_7$, so there are $8$ of them.
